reading.title: Designing with evidence
reading.text: A successful project rarely depends on one clever idea. It develops through observation, testing and decisions that respond to real needs. For this reason, teams should examine the context before choosing a solution. A method that works for one audience may create difficulties for another. Small tests can reveal problems that are difficult to notice from inside the project. They also give people a chance to explain what they actually need. It is important to distinguish between an assumption and evidence. An assumption may be a useful starting point, but it should not replace observation. The strongest approach is therefore flexible: it keeps a clear purpose while remaining open to new evidence.

reading.title: Small changes, lasting effects
reading.text: Creative constraints can feel restrictive at first. Yet a clear limit may help a team focus on the choices that matter most. A practical solution does not have to be the most complicated one. It needs to solve the right problem and remain understandable to the people who use it. Small tests can reveal problems that are difficult to notice from inside the project. They also give people a chance to explain what they actually need. In the end, quality is not simply a matter of appearance; it is the result of thoughtful choices and continuous evaluation.

reading.title: Making feedback useful
reading.text: Feedback can improve a piece of work, but only when comments are specific enough to guide the next decision. For this reason, teams should examine the context before choosing a solution. A method that works for one audience may create difficulties for another. The process takes time, and the first result is not always successful. However, careful revision often produces a clearer and more useful outcome. The strongest approach is therefore flexible: it keeps a clear purpose while remaining open to new evidence.
